defect: The fix makes the external table builder write a RocksDB-generated properties block (new PutPropertiesBlock/GetPropertiesBlock APIs) so SstFileWriter-created external tables can be ingested without allow_db_generated_files.
reason: This is a workflow/feature redesign that adds new external-table APIs, not a repair of a wrong line added by the initial ExternalTableBuilder implementation.

defect: The fix extracts properties-block parsing into a new ParsePropertiesBlock function for the external table ingestion work.
reason: The change only replaced UncompressionDict::GetEmptyDict() with a nullptr decompressor argument; the fix is a refactor/feature unrelated to those lines.

defect: The fix extends the dummy external table test classes with properties-block support and adds ingestion tests.
reason: Test additions for the new ingestion workflow; nothing this change added to the test was wrong.

defect: The change lowered the debug CHECK_TOO_MANY_ITERATIONS assertion limit to 512, which the fix raises to 768 after a suspected false-positive assertion; the fix's main destructor table-size bug is unrelated to this change.
reason: The destructor bug predates this change, and the fix only says the 512 limit 'might' have produced a false positive, so whether this change's threshold is a real defect cannot be established.

defect: The fix updates the include to rocksdb/utilities/options/convenience.h after the header was moved.
reason: The header was moved to include/ by the later commit c1a924b9f the same day as the fix; the include was correct when this change was made.

defect: WriteImplWALOnly now calls DelayWrite() from the nonmem_write_thread_ leader, but DelayWrite stalls the primary write_thread_ (BeginWriteStall) and is not re-entrant, causing LinkOne assertion failures and a stop-writes wake-up deadlock across the two queues.
reason: The fix changes exactly this new call to pass the calling write queue to DelayWrite, and its message attributes the bug to this PR (#11020).

defect: The new header pairs a defaulted virtual base destructor (`virtual ~WriteControllerToken() = default;`) with out-of-line derived destructors, which older supported GCC (4.7) rejects with a 'looser throw specifier' compile error.
reason: The fix (#284) only rewrites these destructor declarations added by this change; the code is standard-valid, so the compiler-specific build failure is not visible from the diff.

defect: The new AppendHumanMicros branch compares against `1000000l * 60 * 60`, which overflows a 32-bit long on i386 (compile error under -Werror=overflow and a wrong threshold).
reason: The fix changes exactly this added constant to 1000000ll.

defect: The fix stops passing the DB pointer to WriteBatchInternal::InsertInto during recovery (unless 2PC), avoiding a mutex deadlock when max_successive_merges triggers a Get().
reason: Passing `this` to InsertInto came from the earlier commit 1b8a2e8 (2PC recovery); this change only added has_valid_writes handling.

defect: The new anonymous-namespace helper IsSectorAligned(size_t, size_t) collides with the identically named function in env/io_posix.cc, breaking the unity build.
reason: The fix renames exactly this added helper to IsFileSectorAligned; the clash is only visible with env/io_posix.cc.

defect: SimpleWriteTimeoutTest relied on min_write_buffer_number_to_merge=3 > max_write_buffer_number to block flushes, but SanitizeOptions clamps it; the fix blocks flushes with a sleeping background task instead.
reason: The premise was already invalid at this change yet the test passed then; it failed only after the later push-model write-stall rewrite (a2bb7c3), and the fix author is himself unsure how it worked, so attribution is unclear.

defect: The new OpenWhenOpen test asserts that the lock error message starts with 'lock ', which only holds for the POSIX env; on Windows the message differs and the test fails (defect in test code).
reason: The fix relaxes exactly this added assertion to a strstr check so it passes with the Windows error text.

defect: WaitingTxn assumes an iteration order of the unordered_multimap returned by GetLockStatusData; the fix makes the check order-independent for Windows.
reason: The order assumption on an unordered container already existed before this change, which only swapped the expected order to match its new sorted insertion; the fix repairs a pre-existing test flaw.

defect: The fix updates the expected NUMBER_ITER_SKIP count in SkipStatistics from 9 to 7 because SeekForPrev now clamps to iterate_upper_bound.
reason: The expectation matched behaviour at the time; the count changed because of the fix's intentional DBIter change, not a defect in this change.

defect: The fix guards FLAGS_use_blob_db uses so ROCKSDB_LITE builds of db_bench compile.
reason: At this change use_blob_db was defined unconditionally; it was moved under #ifndef ROCKSDB_LITE later, so the lite build break was introduced afterwards.

defect: The new BloomSchema test hard-codes the bloom_locality=1 false-positive pattern for CACHE_LINE_SIZE 64, so it fails on platforms where CACHE_LINE_SIZE is 128 or 256 (defect in test code).
reason: The fix replaces exactly this added constant with per-CACHE_LINE_SIZE patterns; the dependency is visible only with port/port_posix.h.

defect: kLen = (total_bits + 8*block_bytes - 1) / 64 does not round the length up to a whole number of blocks, so xor-indexed probes starting in the last words access memory past the allocation.
reason: The fix rewrites exactly this computation to allocate whole blocks after valgrind reported the out-of-bounds access.

defect: SetIsInSecondaryCache() is called after Promote(), when the handle is already inserted into the cache and visible to other threads that modify its flags under the mutex, causing a data race.
reason: The fix moves exactly these added calls before Promote().

defect: FlushSchedule declares `std::atomic<int> thread_num;` without an initializer, so fetch_add reads an indeterminate value (valgrind uninitialized-value error; defect in test code).
reason: The fix initializes exactly this added variable to 0.

defect: The fix replaces the arrays of atomic tickers/histograms with vectors to undo a performance regression caused by D15099 (Statistics code cleanup).
reason: The regression stems from the atomic array introduced by the earlier commit 83681bf and is a performance issue; this change only zero-filled the array.

defect: The new TEST_SYNC_POINT('SstFileManagerImpl::ClearError') fires before RecoverFromBGError(), so the error_handler_test dependency meant to wait until bg_error is cleared races with recovery and fails intermittently (test-only effect).
reason: The fix moves exactly this added sync point after RecoverFromBGError; the race is visible only with db/error_handler_test.cc.

defect: The fix renames the sync point to 'CompactionJob::Run():Inprogress' to match the renamed Start/End sync points used by the test.
reason: At this change the sync point names were consistent with the test; a later commit (c594b0e/8c12426) renamed the others and broke the dependency.

defect: The fix updates DynamicLevelMaxBytesBase2 to the renamed 'CompactionJob::Run():Start' sync point.
reason: The sync point name was correct when this change was made; a later rename broke it.

defect: The new log line prints live_wal_files.size() (size_t) with '%ld', a format/argument mismatch that is undefined behaviour and a -Wformat error where size_t is not long.
reason: The fix replaces exactly this added format with ROCKSDB_PRIszt.

defect: BackupFileTemperature opens a BackupEngine through a raw pointer and never deletes it, leaking memory (valgrind failure; defect in test code).
reason: The fix wraps exactly this added BackupEngine in a unique_ptr.

defect: The new condition `!FLAGS_avoid_flush_during_shutdown` is inverted: it skips SyncWAL exactly when shutdown does not flush and recovery depends on the WAL, causing false data-loss failures in the crash test.
reason: The fix flips exactly this added condition; the inversion contradicts the change's own stated intent.

defect: Meaning to give Directory::Close a default, the change instead turned WritableFile::Close from pure virtual into a NotSupported default, silently changing the WritableFile interface contract.
reason: The fix reverts exactly this line to `= 0` and moves the default to Directory::Close, calling the WritableFile edit a mistake.

defect: FSDirectory::Close is added as a new pure virtual method of a public interface, breaking compilation of existing user FSDirectory implementations (not backward compatible).
reason: The fix replaces exactly this pure virtual with a default NotSupported implementation.

defect: The fix adds the WriteBuffer argument to the MemTable constructor call in the JNI test helper to repair the Java build.
reason: The MemTable constructor gained the WriteBuffer parameter in a later commit; the call compiled when this change was made.

defect: DestroyDB propagates the error from DeleteDir on the archive directory, so it returns failure when no archive directory exists (WAL_ttl_seconds = 0).
reason: The fix ignores exactly this added DeleteDir status.

defect: The fix replaces sprintf into the 19-byte writelen_temp buffer with snprintf to address lint warnings.
reason: Both formatted strings fit in 19 bytes for every reachable value (uint32 checksum, files_.size() far below 10^17), so the fix is lint hardening rather than repair of a reachable overrun.

defect: ASSERT_EQ(0, arena.ApproximateMemoryUsage()) compares an int with a size_t, a sign-compare warning that breaks the build under -Wall -Werror (test code).
reason: The fix changes exactly this added assertion to compare against a size_t zero.

defect: The fix makes env_test build on Windows (aligned allocation helper and excluding the O_DIRECT sync-point callbacks).
reason: The O_DIRECT callbacks and posix_memalign usage came from the earlier Direct IO commit f89caa1; this change only wrapped them for macOS.

defect: New assertions compare int values with size_t GetUsage() (e.g. ASSERT_EQ(1, cache_->GetUsage()), ASSERT_EQ(n + 1, ...)), producing sign-compare errors under -Werror on macOS (test code).
reason: The fix changes exactly these added assertions and variables to unsigned types.

defect: The fix strips the user-defined-timestamp placeholder from keys when rebuilding a recovered prepared transaction from its WriteBatch.
reason: The bug already existed in PutCF/DeleteCF/MergeCF before this change, and the newly added PutEntityCF cannot meet timestamped keys because WriteBatch::PutEntity rejects timestamp-enabled column families.

defect: The fix stops printing tolerated or injected errors to stdout and renames IsRetryableInjectedError.
reason: Logging cleanup and refactor; the tolerated-status logic added by this change is unchanged.

defect: The fix renames IsRetryableInjectedError to IsErrorInjectedAndRetryable and asserts the status is not OK.
reason: Rename/refactor accompanying logging reduction; the helper added by this change did not behave wrongly.

defect: The fix removes verbose logging of retryable injected errors in the stress test.
reason: Logging cleanup in code unrelated to this MultiGetEntity refactor; no defect is repaired.

defect: The test picks compression_types[0] from GetSupportedCompressions(), which always includes kNoCompression in unspecified map order, so compression can be silently disabled and the MultiGet test fails (e.g. on Windows CI; defect in test code).
reason: The fix replaces exactly this added selection with the first type other than kNoCompression; the ordering issue is visible only in options/options_helper.cc.

defect: start_time is set only in the timed-delay branch, so when a write is delayed only by the stop-writes wait loop, time_delayed = NowMicros() - 0 records a huge bogus stall time.
reason: The fix moves exactly this added start_time initialization before the branch.
